summary: Pairing a phone can grant it the member's client gateway over Fabric, when the person asks for it for that pairing, and revoking the pairing removes the grant: after `st devices fabric enable` exposes the paired-only client socket once, a code made with `st devices pair NAME --fabric-gateway` takes the phone's Fabric NodeID, the member runs `fabric add NODE st-device-… --inbound-only --allow SERVICE`, and `st devices revoke` runs `fabric remove`; `st devices fabric status` and `disable` show and undo it. A pairing made without `--fabric-gateway` grants nothing.

replay.detail: Replay is unchanged. The pairing-completed claim carries an optional fabric_node_id field that older readers ignore.

schema.detail: Client v0: PersonPairingBegin takes an optional fabric_gateway, PairingComplete an optional fabric_node_id, PairedSession may carry fabric_grant (granted, already-trusted, not-enabled, not-requested or failed), and the anonymous pairing advertisement lists fabric-gateway-grant version 1 only when the request carries `?accepts=fabric-gateway-grant`; any other request gets the single device-key-proofs entry it always has. No database schema change; new optional fields on the custom.client.pairing-begun and pairing-completed claims.

rules.detail: Checkpoint rules and fleet coordination are unchanged.

compatibility.detail: Off unless the person asks: nothing is granted for a pairing made without `--fabric-gateway`, and nothing at all on a member without `st devices fabric enable`. The advertisement older clients validate is unchanged (one entry) unless the client asks for the second; the phone asks, sends fabric_node_id only to a member that then lists fabric-gateway-grant, so an older member, which refuses unknown pairing fields, never sees it. An older phone pairs as before and gets no grant. st changes only Fabric peers named st-device-… that it added, never a grant made by hand. Granting needs fabric 0.2.41 or later on the member; on an older fabric the grant fails, the pairing stands, and the phone says so.

downtime.detail: No restart beyond the ordinary daemon update.

manual.detail: Optional, once per member that should serve phones over Fabric: `st devices fabric enable`. It replaces the manual `fabric expose` and per-phone `fabric add`. A grant someone made by hand stays and still needs removing by hand.

recovery.detail: Run `st devices fabric disable` to remove st's grants and the exposure, then revert the commit. A reverted daemon ignores STATE/fabric-gateway.toml.
